newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: GOLF-HOCH LEADS BY ONE SHOT AS THIRD ROUND AT MEMORIAL SUSPENDED.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-HOCH LEADS BY ONE SHOT AS THIRD ROUND AT MEMORIAL SUSPENDED.

text.p: Third round play in the Memorial tournament was suspended due to heavy rain Saturday that made the Muirfield Village course unplayable with leader Scott Hoch able to play just three holes.
Play was scheduled to resume, weather permitting, early Sunday morning with the fourth round then following on Sunday afternoon.
Hoch, the second-round leader at 12 under par, bogeyed the first two holes on Saturday to slip to 10 under.

Tied for second place at nine under were Tommy Tolles and Vijay Singh of Fiji, both also having finished three holes. Tolles, who started the day at 10-under, bogeyed a hole while Singh parred the first three holes to remain at nine under.
The forecast is for more rain, and if they are not able to play Sunday morning tournament officials will decide whether to shorten the tournament to 36 or 54 holes, or resume play on Monday.
Playing Monday would interfere with the USGA's second stage of U.S. Open qualifying. Of those who made the cut, 18 are scheduled to go through Monday's 36-hole qualifier in nearby Columbus.
Bob Tway birdied four of the first six holes before his round was suspended to move to eight under. Lee Janzen birdied one of his first three holes to tie Tway at minus eight.

The biggest surprise of the rain-plagued Memorial has been the sudden slump of Tiger Woods. Woods, who carded a 75 Friday to barely make the cut at three-over, had a birdie and a bogey thorugh five holes on Saturday.
Woods was in a group with John Daley, making his first start since undergoing a round of alcoholism treatment. Daley bogeyed three of his first four holes Saturday to drop to six-over.
